text: Projection profiles should be openly published and selected locally by relying parties because a specification body that controls both evidence schema and canonical scoring holds unrecorded allocative power.
scope_conditions: Persona Protocol v0.3 as proposed; not an adopted standard
supporting_quote: Governance of the projection profile deserves separate treatment because it is the locus of capture. A specification body that controls both the evidence schema and the canonical scoring rule holds allocative power that no authority grant records. The failure pattern is well documented: recentralization is the central obstacle to decentralized governance of AI systems (Kaal 2024a, claim 4796714-012), and consensus mechanisms that weight power by holdings "centralize control based on the quantity of tokens held, potentially skewing governance in favor of the wealthy" (Kaal 2024a, claim 4796714-014). Persona Protocol therefore treats profile publication as open and profile selection as local to the relying party.

source.title: Persona Protocol: Continuity, Competence, Trust, and Authority for Autonomous Systems
